NCERT Class 12 Contemporary World Politics (Chapter 2: The End of Bipolarity, 'Timeline of Soviet Disintegration', p. 23): (A) The Berlin Wall, which symbolised the Cold War, was toppled in November 1989 (Match IV). (B) Russia took over the USSR seat in the United Nations in December 1991 as the legal successor state (Match III). (C) Russian parliament declared independence/sovereignty from the Soviet Union in June 1990 (Match II). (D) Mikhail Gorbachev appointed Boris Yeltsin as head of the Communist Party in Moscow in 1985 (Match I). Matching: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I).
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

(A) Fall of the Berlin Wall
(B) Soviet intervention in Afghanistan

1. Soviet invasion of Afghanistan occurred in 1979 (B).

Chronology of the disintegration of the Soviet Union:
1. (C) Lithuania became the first Soviet republic to declare independence: March 1990.
2. (B) Russian parliament declared sovereignty/independence from USSR: June 1990.
3. (D) Boris Yeltsin elected President of the Russian Federation: June 1991.
4. (A) Mikhail Gorbachev resigned as President of the Soviet Union: 25 December 1991.
Correct order: (C), (B), (D), (A).
